FICTIONAL TEST DOCUMENT. Imran Sheikh versus State. The accused sought regular bail in a case of alleged fraud involving forged land records. He had been in custody for over two years while the trial had not commenced, and only three of the forty listed prosecution witnesses had been examined. The court reiterated that bail is the rule and jail is the exception, and that prolonged incarceration of an undertrial without any likelihood of the trial concluding soon infringes the right to personal liberty. The State's objection that the accused might tamper with evidence was rejected because the documentary evidence was already seized. Bail was granted on furnishing a bond of one lakh rupees with two sureties, subject to the condition that the accused surrenders his passport and reports to the investigating officer every Monday.
